segmentation.text: speed contest or exhibition of power or speed
no person shall aid or abet in

elements.justification: Engaging is read through the subject vehicle's own conduct: kin.accel_longitudinal 'acceleration along heading, signed' ('Not a stand-in for: speed' respected: both are read separately) and kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity'. The person who engages is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The contest is one in a motor vehicle, so the subject is a member; the other party of a contest is a member too.

st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; the subject is on it where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' does not apply: the words name the highway.

operationalizations.standard: speed contest or exhibition of power or speed
operationalizations.convention: naturalistic-driving harsh-event thresholds: an exhibition of power is a longitudinal acceleration above a harsh-acceleration threshold, an exhibition of speed a speed above a bound far beyond any posted limit, and a contest two motor vehicles side by side in the same direction both accelerating above a lower threshold throughout a window

applicability: The subject, a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle), occupies a highway region (st.highway, rel.occupies).
obligation: Not any of: (a) the subject's kin.accel_longitudinal is at least p.exhibition_accel_min; (b) its kin.speed is at least p.exhibition_speed_min; (c) at every observation of the time window p.contest_window behind, some other road user o that is a motor vehicle (same aggregate) has rel.same_direction(subject, o; p.contest_same_direction_cos), positive rel.longitudinal_overlap with the subject, and both the subject's and o's kin.accel_longitudinal are at least p.contest_accel_min (o bound inside the window, one road user throughout).

narrowings.why: 'person ... engage' is read through the controlled motion of the motor vehicle the person drives

a contest or exhibition is a purpose shown in conduct; it is read only through acceleration, speed and side-by-side acceleration with another motor vehicle; burnouts, wheel spin and sliding manoeuvres are not read

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two motor vehicles side by side in the same direction on a highway both accelerating above p.contest_accel_min for the whole p.contest_window.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject accelerates moderately from a light, below every bound, alone in its direction.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is in a private parking lot that is no highway region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Accelerations are not observed and the subject's speed is below the speed bound.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No other road user in the scene; the subject alone accelerates above p.exhibition_accel_min (exhibition of power).

param_proposals.name: p.exhibition_accel_min
param_proposals.convention: harsh-acceleration threshold: a longitudinal acceleration of about 0.4 g, beyond ordinary driving
param_proposals.source: naturalistic driving studies' harsh-event thresholds (e.g. SHRP2, 100-Car study)

param_proposals.name: p.exhibition_speed_min
param_proposals.convention: a speed of about 100 mph, beyond any posted limit in the jurisdiction
param_proposals.source: highest posted limits in Nevada (80 mph) plus a margin

param_proposals.name: p.contest_accel_min
param_proposals.convention: a sustained acceleration well above ordinary launches (about 0.25 g) held by both vehicles

param_proposals.name: p.contest_window
param_proposals.convention: duration a side-by-side hard acceleration must last to be a contest rather than a merge

param_proposals.name: p.contest_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 18 degrees) for travel in the same direction
